problem: Improve contact-rich policies while correcting the optimistic bias of world models trained mainly on successful demonstrations.
contribution: VLAW alternates fresh physical rollout collection, world/reward adaptation, synthetic success selection and flow-policy regression. It explicitly measures interaction outcomes in addition to video fidelity, making failure coverage central to the method.
algorithm: Initialize pi0.5/Ctrl-World; append actual policy successes/failures and co-train world model withDROID. Fine-tune Qwen3VL4B reward on first-round outcome labels and filter generated trajectories by yes-token probability. Update policy on successful real plus imagined episodes using flow matching. Binary success weighting is described as an approximation to regularized advantage-weighted RL, not a complete policy-gradient method.
observations: Two third-person and one wrist camera with robot action sequences; sparse success label assigned at each real reset. Wrist video metrics and event-level confusion are separate evaluations. World-model outputs remain hypotheses even after adaptation.
actions: DROID FrankaPanda/Robotiq action convention; pi0.5 flow chunks. No new morphology/action-head conversion is provided. Synthetic rollout starts are sampled from actual observed trajectories.
embodiment_and_data: Five real categories:stacking,book opening,whiteboard erasing,scooping,drawing.25expert demonstrations/category for policy warmstart; each of2rounds adds50real rollouts/category,50k world-model updates,500synthetic trajectories/category and2kpolicy steps,batch256. Actual target collection cost is material.
experiments: Compare pretrained/expert-only/online-adapted video replay on256five-second wrist clips;50interaction clips get success/failure confusion matrix. Compare filtered realBC andDSRL at equal50real-rollout/category budget. Drawing ablates synthetic quantity and real-success inclusion.
baselines: Ctrl-World,expert-only finetuned model; filteredBC andDSRL with matched online count. Policy iteration uses different refined-policy data each round; it is not pure offline improvement with no new physical data.
quantitative_result: Table1 PDFp6 event confusion expert-onlyTP28,FN2,TN9,FP11 versuswithonlineTP26,FN4,TN19,FP1 over50clips: false positives improve while false negatives worsen. Figure9p8 drawing first-round22%base,46%real-only,50%synthetic-only,60%halfsynthetic+real,68%fullmix. Figure7p7 mean labels46base,50DSRL,64/75filteredBCrounds,74/86VLAWrounds; exact physical evaluation denominator NOT_EXTRACTED.
limitations: Five task categories only; quality depends on local online data and reward threshold. Success filtering can propagate model/reward bias and discard useful failures for policy training. Interaction confusion still has errors; visual similarity is insufficient. High synthetic volume and broadDROID co-training costs should be accounted for.
code_and_license: Independent repository, weights and data-license inspection not performed; Ctrl-World/pi0.5/Qwen/DROID rights are separate. No code inspected/executed.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT event-level real-versus-predicted confusion logging and typed success/failure datasets. Small independent target experiments should compare real-only and mixed data under identical collection budgets. Neither current geometry adapter nor recorded camera demonstration is a VLAW-trained model; keep controllers unchanged.
